Civil and Environmental Engineering
Civil and Environmental Engineering
Apply
Civil engineering education at MU began in 1856 with the establishment of the first Chair of Civil Engineering. Graduate programs offered by the department prepare students for leadership positions in academia, research and advanced practice engineering careers. Major program areas include structural mechanics, structural engineering and materials, geotechnical and geoenvironmental engineering, environmental engineering, hydrology and water resources engineering and transportation engineering.

*This is a recommended application deadline. We will consider applications to the start of the semester.
This accelerated master’s program is open to current MU undergraduate students who meet the admissions requirements below.
Applicants must:
Have completed, or be on track to complete, at least 90 credit hours toward a bachelor’s in Civil Engineering or related fields.
Meet the following admissions requirements:
Have earned a cumulative GPA 3.0.
Have earned a GPA of 3.0 or higher in each of the introductory courses of the selected area of emphasis, such as:
CE 3100 Fundamental of Transportation Engineering for Transportation.
CE 3200 Fundamentals of Environmental Engineering or CE 3702 Hydrology for Environmental/Water resources.
CE 3300 Structural Analysis I for Structures.
CE 3400 Fundamental of Geotechnical Engineering for Geotechnical.
Have completed all general education requirements.

Construction Management, Graduate Certificate
Graduate Certificate
|
100% Online
Officially approved as:
Stand Alone: Yes
Total Credit Hours: 12
Certificate description: The primary objective of the Graduate Certificate in Construction Management is to position students and professionals to succeed in the construction industry. The construction industry builds the basic infrastructure necessary to sustain modern cities and communities. Examples of such infrastructure include highways, bridges, hospitals, powerlines, and water treatment plants. The successful delivery of such infrastructure requires skillful project managers to navigate the various steps of the project delivery process. Certificate holders will acquire experience in various aspects of CM such as planning, environmental compliance, design, right-of-way acquisition, estimation, resource management, financing, and scheduling.
